blockers.title: EXTERNAL-ORIGIN is simultaneously origin-only and volume-required
evidence: The new closed union gives EXTERNAL-ORIGIN a laterEventVariant containing only observedOrigin. volumeConstraint rejects cross-tag fields, and retainedEventSchema points volumeObservation to these per-tag variants.

The unchanged laterEventVolumeFields remains required when volumeConstraint is INSTALL-ROOT-VOLUME or EXTERNAL-ORIGIN, and its required list contains observedVolumeIdentity and observedFilesystemTypeToken; Linux additionally requires linuxSelectedMountRecordIdentity.

The unchanged evidenceJoin still defines only INSTALL-ROOT and PATHLESS joins and still routes INSTALL-ROOT through laterEventVolumeFields. It has no EXTERNAL-ORIGIN join, while volumeEquality separately says EXTERNAL must join canonicalOrigin/observedOrigin and must not use install-root volume equality.

An EXTERNAL-ORIGIN event therefore cannot satisfy both retained schemas: the closed union permits only observedOrigin, while laterEventVolumeFields requires cross-tag volume fields that the union rejects. No supersession or precedence clause retires laterEventVolumeFields, and evidenceJoin still references it.
blockers.impact: A declared external system dependency has no conforming retained event. One verifier can reject the required volume fields as illegal extras while another can reject their absence, so the contract cannot deterministically qualify the external-origin branch that exists to represent host/system dependencies outside the install volume.
blockers.requiredRepair: Replace or explicitly retire laterEventVolumeFields and make evidenceJoin exhaustive over the same three variants as volumeConstraint. Define one authoritative EXTERNAL-ORIGIN event with observedOrigin, its canonicalization/equality rule, and its allowedLoaderOrSearchOrder join; forbid install-root volume fields there. Reject extras once, in that single schema.

shouldFix.title: The run-level preselection record is not a closed, subject-bound retained record
evidence: runPreselectionRecord says exactly one exists per qualification runIdentity and that later events join by runIdentity, but runIdentity is absent from requiredAtObservation and no enclosing run map or key schema supplies it.

Later events retain subjectDigest and allowlistOrCarrierDigest, while the run-level record requires neither subjectDigest nor a carrier digest. A baseline can therefore be associated with later events without a defined retained equality binding to the subject and signed carrier whose root it measured.

The record has no eventTime or sequenceAndClosure equivalent and no extras-rejected rule, so retained bytes do not prove the record preceded profile selection or define its exhaustive shape. Forbidding completePlatformProfileKey at observation time does not supply that missing ordering/binding evidence.

evidenceJoin remains byte-for-byte in the event model and says exactly one preselection event exists per runIdentity even though v14 removes preselection from eventKind and declares the record not to be an event.
shouldFix.impact: An independent verifier cannot establish from the closed retained evidence that exactly one baseline belongs to this run, subject, and carrier and was captured before selection. Baseline substitution or retrospective attachment remains structurally possible.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define a closed qualification-run container or closed runPreselectionRecord carrying runIdentity, subjectDigest, the signed-carrier digest, and an observation sequence/time binding before selection, with exact Linux/macOS variants and extras rejected. Update evidenceJoin to name runPreselectionRecord, not a preselection event, and bind every later event to those exact fields.

shouldFix.title: The claimed closed tag and identity serializations remain non-canonical
evidence: The new signedObject forms place canonicalOrigin inside the EXTERNAL-ORIGIN object and pathlessObservation inside the PATHLESS object, while originSearchPolicy continues to define canonicalOrigin and pathlessObservation as sibling fields. The contract does not say whether the nested values replace, reference, duplicate, or must equal the siblings.

runPreselectionRecord still declares only volumeIdentity (OS-tagged). macOS f_fsid, the Linux decoded-mount-point/device pair, and linuxSelectedMountRecordIdentity remain prose labels without exact field names, scalar types, encodings, or canonical serialized objects.

The PATHLESS observedAttestation and EXTERNAL observedOrigin are field names only; neither has a retained value shape or equality/canonicalization algorithm. volumeEquality nevertheless claims that each OS-tagged identity has a closed form on the INSTALL-ROOT variant, whose laterEventVariant is only a list of names.
shouldFix.impact: Producers can sign different field layouts and encode or compare OS identities, origins, and attestations differently while claiming the same contract. The retained evidence is named but not byte- or type-exact, so independent replay is not deterministic.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Choose one signed location for canonicalOrigin and pathlessObservation and define exact exhaustive objects for all three tags. Specify canonical retained macOS and Linux identity objects, linuxSelectedMountRecordIdentity, observedAttestation, and observedOrigin, including types, normalization/decoding, equality, required/forbidden fields, and extras rejection.

shouldFix.title: Holding procfs descriptors does not bind the namespace handle and mount table to one snapshot
evidence: The protocol opens /proc/<pid>/stat, /proc/<pid>/ns/mnt, and /proc/<pid>/mountinfo and then holds them, but it gives no acquisition order or check that the ns/mnt and mountinfo descriptors were opened against the same mount namespace.

A live process can retain the same {pid,starttime} while changing mount namespaces between those distinct opens. Both descriptors remain valid, no ESRCH or ESTALE is required, and the before/after process pair remains equal, yet the retained namespace inode can describe namespace A while the selected mountinfo record describes namespace B.

The contract itself says inode equality alone does not exclude an A-to-B-to-A transition. A dedicated verifier or frozen/coordinated target is merely permitted, not required, and linuxSelectedMountRecordIdentity does not prove that its record came from the namespace represented by the held ns/mnt descriptor.
shouldFix.impact: A conforming implementation can retain a fabricated composite namespace identity and install-volume baseline. Later equality then compares against that composite rather than a reproducible process/namespace snapshot.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Require a stable acquisition protocol that binds all three observations to one task and one mount namespace: for example, require a dedicated immutable or frozen target and derive mountinfo through the held namespace, or validate the held namespace identity throughout descriptor acquisition with an equivalent fail-closed handshake. Retain the binding evidence and reject any acquisition transition.

advisories.title: The superseded single-domain verified-root equality sentence remains in the live schema
advisories.evidence: signedBinding.serialization.equality still says UTF-8 byte equality is evaluated after NFC and after canonicalization, conflating the signed token with the host-local path. verifiedInstallRoot.equality now correctly splits signedTokenBytes from hostLocalCanonicalPath, and supersedesPriorEquality explicitly gives the split clause precedence.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The new supersession sentence makes the operative two-domain comparison unambiguous, so this stale sentence need not change an allow/refuse result; it remains misleading normative debris.
advisories.suggestedRepair: Delete the old equality sentence or replace it with an explicit pointer to tcbCarrier.verifiedInstallRoot.equality.
